Bankey Lal M/s Bhartiya Manav Kalyan Parishad Truck No. Dl1Ls6615 Parked in Police Station Harsh Vihar, Delhi110093 . R/o F30, East Jyoti Nagar Delhi93. F.B.O.cum-CoOrdinator Mid Day Meal Accused No.1 2. Sh. Harish Kumar S/o Sh. Kanchan Pal M/s Bhartiya Manav Kalyan Parishad Unit at: Khasra No. 15/15 Main Sewadham Road, Mandoli, Delhi110093. Having Regd. Office at: PattyMeher, Baraut District Baghpat, Up250611 R/o D1/78, Ashok Nagar Extn. Delhi93
texts.facts: 1. Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the present appeal filed by the appellants against the impugned order dated 19.12.2018, whereby the Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (East), Delhi, imposed a penalty of Rs.30,000/ under Sections 50 & 51 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (in short 'the FSS Act') upon each of the appellants. 2. The facts in brief are that on 09.12.2015 at about 06:30pm, Sh. Bijandera Pal Saroha, Food Safety Officer, took a sample of 'Sugar' for analysis from Sh. Chakresh Aggarwal S/o Sh. Bankey Lal, FBO/Appellant No. 1 M/s Bharatiya Manav Kalyan Parishad, Harsh Vihar, Delhi110 093. The said food article was stated to be ready for use. The FSO tried to associate some public witnesses by requesting customers and passersby but none came forward. Thereafter, the FSO requested Sh. Rajpal Singh, the then Field Assistant to join the proceedings as witness, to which he agreed. The FSO purchased a sample of 'Sugar' for analysis from the FBO/Appellant No. 1 and a credit note dated 09.12.2015 was prepared on the spot for payment of sample price but the sample price was not accepted. Thereafter, the sample of food article was divided into four equal counterparts and put in four clean and dry bottles. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed as per the provisions of the FSS Act/Rules & Regulations. Notice in Form VA was prepared at the spot and copy of the same was given to the FBO/Appellant No. 1. On 10.12.2015, one counterpart of the aforesaid sample was sent to the Food Analyst. The other two counterparts were deposited with the Designated Officer Sh. O.P.S. Ahlawat. As the FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis to NABL accredited laboratory, it was deposited with the Designated Officer. 3. The Food Analyst vide his report No. FSS/1254/2016 dated 14.12.2015 opined that the sample is unsafe because it is not free from insects. The Food Analyst further opined that the sample is also substandard because moisture exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 0.5% be weight and Sucrose content is less than the prescribed limit of 98.0% be weight. 4. The FBO was given an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of Food Analyst. The FBO preferred an appeal and one sample counterpart was sent to the Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore. The Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore, vide report No. 26F/FSSA/2016 dated 11.04.2016 opined that the sample is "Substandard" as defined under Section 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006 as it does not conform to the standards laid down for Plantation White Sugar under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011. texts.arguments: Sh. Kundan Lal, Ld. Chief PP for the State has submitted that the Ld. AO/ADM has rightly imposed the penalty upon the appellants, as the sample of the food article was found to be substandard. In support of his arguments, Ld. Chief PP for the State has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Delhi Administration vs. Vidya Gupta, Crl. Appeal No. 625/2018, decided on 24.04.2018. 7. Ld. Chief PP for the State has further submitted that in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Delhi Administration vs. Vidya Gupta (Supra), it is clear that the subsequent report of the RFL shall supersede the earlier report of the Public Analyst. Ld. Chief PP for the State further submitted that in the documents, prepared on the spot at the time of taking the sample, it was specifically mentioned that the sample taken was of 'sugar'. The technical name of 'plantation sugar' is generally mentioned only at the time of analysis. It has further been submitted that at that time, the appellants had also not taken any plea that it was 'khandsari sugar'. 8. Per contra, Sh. R.D. Goel, Ld. Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the Ld. AO/ADM has passed the order mechanically. It has been submitted that the Food Analyst as well as the Director, RFL, have not done characteristic tests to found out whether it was plantation white sugar or it was Khandsari Sugar. Ld. Counsel further submitted that even in the documents prepared at the time of taking samples, it was not mentioned that it was plantation white sugar. Ld. Counsel submitted that in fact, it was khandsari sugar. It has been further submitted that in plantation white sugar, the sucrose content should be 98%, but in the Khandsari Sugar, it was 93.8%. The report of the Food Analyst and Director, RFL are highly divergent, hence, the sample was not taken in representative manner and the benefit of the doubt should be given to the appellants. In support of his arguments, Ld. Counsel for the appellants has relied upon the following judgment : 1. Delhi Administration vs. Kishan Lal Nagpal Crl. L.P. No. 207/2014, decided on 11.03.2014; 2. M.V. Krishna Nambissan vs. State of Kerala 19481997 SC FAC 522; 3. MCD vs. Ram Kishan 1985 (II) FAC 192 Delhi High Court; 4. Food Inspector vs. Rajender Rathore & Ors. 2015(2) FAC 385 Delhi High Court; 5. DA vs. Kishan Lal Nagpal Supreme Court of India vide case no. 20201/2014; 6. DA vs. Prabhu Dayal SLP No. 7905/2014 decided on 03.01.2017; 7. Delhi Admn. vs. Sunil Kumar Khemani & Ors. 9. Noratan Mal vs. State of Rajasthan Supreme Court of India 19481997 FAC 996; 10. Kanshi Nath vs. State 2005(2) FAC 219 Delhi High Court; 11. Delhi Administration vs. Mahender Mahajan Crl. LP No. 132 of 2014 Delhi High Court; 12. Food Inspector vs. Dinesh Kumar 2014(2) FAC 274 Delhi High Court; 13. Food Inspector vs. Dinesh Goswami 2014(1) FAC 302 Delhi High Court; 14. State vs. Phul Chand & Anr. 2014(2) FAC 144 Delhi High Court; and 15. Food Inspector vs. Sanjay Aggarwal 2014(2) FAC 285 Delhi High Court; 10. The Food Analyst as well as Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore have opined that the sample of food article is substandard. In State of Kerala Vs. Parameswaram Pillai Vasudevan Nair, 1975 Cri LJ 97, it was interalia held as under : "14. The Act is a piece of consumer legislation. It regulates to some extent the consumersupplier relations. Consumerists demand enforcement of discipline among the producers or manufacturers of food to ensure safety in the realm of food. The consumer's legitimate ignorance and his almost total dependence on the fairness and competence of those who supply his daily needs have made him a ready target for exploitation. The Act is intended to protect him against outright frauds. It does not provide for aggravation of offence based on the extent of contamination. Food pollution, even if it be only to the slightest extent, if continued in practice, would adversely affect the health of every man, woman and child in the country. The disadvantages of the resulting unpredictability, uncertainty and Sh. Charkesh Aggarwal vs Fso Page 1 Of 15 on 8 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162467825/ 4 impossibility of arriving at fair and consistent decisions, are great. 18. The standards of qualities of the articles have been fixed by the Government under the provisions of the Act after due deliberation and after consulting a committee of competent men. Therefore the conclusion is that for an article of food when a standard has been fixed under the Act it has to be observed in every detail." 11. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Delhi Administration vs. Vidya Gupta (Supra), interalia held as under : "This section must be construed according to the rule of interpretation enunciated in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Kacheroo Mal (1976) 1 SCC 412, which also arose under this Act. This Court enunciated the Rule as follows: "5. The Act has been enacted to curb and remedy the widespread evil of food adulteration, and to ensure the sale of wholesome food to the people. It is well settled that wherever possible, without unreasonable stretching or straining, the language of such a statute should be construed in a manner which would suppress the mischief, advance the remedy, promote its object, prevent its subtle evasion and foil its artful circumvention......." 12. In respect to the variation of the report of Food Analyst and Director, Referral Food Laboratory, it was inter alia held as under : "8. Section 13 lays down the procedure by which the report of the PA that an article of food is adulterated is dealt with. In brief the procedure is as follows: When a report, that the article of food is adulterated, is received and a prosecution is instituted, the local health authority is enjoined to forward a copy of the report of such analysis to such person or persons who may have applied for having such food analyzed vide Section 12. Such persons may, if desired, make an application to the Court to have the sample of the article of food analysed by the Director, and the Court may then dispatch a part of the sample received to the Director. The Director shall send a certificate specifying the result of the analysis. Sh. Charkesh Aggarwal vs Fso Page 1 Of 15 on 8 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162467825/ 5 9. It reads as follows: "13. Report of public analyst (1) .............. (2) ............... (2A).............. (2B).............. (2C).............. (2D).............. (2E).............. (3) The certificate issued by the Director of the Central Food Laboratory [under sub section(2B)] shall supersede the report given by the public analyst under subsection (1)." 11. Moreover, this view is no more res integra in view of the judgment of this Court in Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf and another (1999) 2 SCC 400. This Court held as follows: "Per majority (Thomas and Quadri, JJ.) When Section 13(3) says that the certificate of Director, CFL shall supersede the report, it means that the report would stand annulled or obliterated. The word "supersede" in law means "obliterate, [LEAKAGE_MASK], annul, replace, make void or inefficacious or useless, repeal". Once the certificate of the Director of the Central Food Laboratory Sh. Charkesh Aggarwal vs Fso Page 1 Of 15 on 8 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162467825/ 6 reaches the court, the report of the Public Analyst stands displaced and what may remain is only a fossil of it. It annuls or replaces the report of the Public Analyst, it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned." 13.
